name: Waxahatchee
label: Anti-
lede: A teenager from Birmingham started with a cassette named for a creek, and two decades later her sixth album is one of the year's critics' favorites.

eras.title: Two sisters, one Birmingham basement
eras.text: Twin sisters Katie and Allison Crutchfield start playing out as teenagers in Alabama and never really stop. By 2011 they have two bands behind them and a songwriter ready to go it alone.

years.h: The Ackleys: the Crutchfield twins start a band in Alabama
years.p: Katie and Allison Crutchfield, born January 4, 1989, form the Ackleys and put out a self-titled album and the EP Forget Forget, Derive Derive.
years.xp: By the time Katie was 17 she was playing Cave9, a Birmingham all-ages room, nearly every week, according to Grantland's 2015 profile. The Ackleys were where the sisters learned to tour on nothing, a habit that never left Katie's career.

years.h: P.S. Eliot replaces the Ackleys, and Katie writes everything
years.p: The sisters restart as [[P.S. Eliot|97017fae-cdcd-47f1-843d-4a69a81675ed]] with Will Granger and Katherine Simonetti, touring the US on a DIY circuit and releasing on Salinas Records.
years.xp:
P.S. Eliot made Introverted Romance in Our Troubled Minds (2009, Salinas), the Living in Squalor EP (2010, Freedom School) and Sadie (2011, Salinas). Katie later told an interviewer she drove every decision in the band, including writing all the songs.

That lopsided authorship is the obvious reason the next project would carry her name alone, or close to it.

years.h: P.S. Eliot play their farewell at Death By Audio in Brooklyn
years.p: The band calls it after four years, with members in different cities and wanting different music.
years.xp: Allison had already moved to Philadelphia, where she started [[Swearin'|5b62be91-b158-40a7-a51d-43b1a3b91ec3]] with Kyle Gilbride, Keith Spencer and Jeff Bolt. Katie went the other way, back to Alabama, and kept writing.

eras.title: A creek, a cassette and a breakthrough
eras.text: Waxahatchee starts as a bedroom record and turns into the most talked-about songwriter project on Don Giovanni. The sound gets a band by the second album, borrowed from her sister's.

years.h: Waxahatchee starts as a cassette, named for a creek
years.p: While P.S. Eliot is still active, Katie Crutchfield releases her first solo songs on cassette as Waxahatchee, after Waxahatchee Creek, near where she grew up in Alabama.

years.h: American Weekend: one week of songs, one borrowed microphone
years.p: Don Giovanni puts out the debut, a bedroom record written and recorded in about a week at her family home in Birmingham.
years.xp:
Grantland's account has the songs coming over seven winter days after a breakup, and Wikipedia says it was recorded in a week at her family's house. NPR picked "Be Good" as a Song of the Day in June 2012 and later put it among its 50 favorite songs of the year.

The Times and Dusted both named it a top album of 2012. Paste placed it No. 238 on its 2025 list of the best albums of the century so far.

years.cap: Waxahatchee at Huichica Walla Walla in 2019 · Wikimedia
years.h: Cerulean Salt, made in a West Philly basement
years.p: Recorded September to November 2012, Katie works with Allison, Kyle Gilbride and Keith Spencer of [[Swearin'|5b62be91-b158-40a7-a51d-43b1a3b91ec3]] and Sam Cook-Parrott, and the record finally sounds like a band.
years.xp: Released March 5, 2013 on Don Giovanni in the US and Wichita in the UK. Pitchfork's Lindsay Zoladz called it the work of a songwriter "skilled enough to make introspection not self-centered, but generous." Pitchfork gave it 8.4 with Best New Music and ranked it No. 22 of 2013.

years.h: Waxahatchee heads to the UK, then tops the record store chart
years.p: A UK tour supporting Tegan and Sara is followed by a headline run in October, and Cerulean Salt reaches No. 1 on the Official Record Store Chart in July.

eras.title: Merge Records and the loud years
eras.text: A bigger label, a bigger sound and a record about what all that touring was doing to her. Katie trades the four-track for a band and a proper studio.

years.h: Ivy Tripp: a year on Long Island, and a move to Merge
years.p: She leaves Don Giovanni for Merge and spends nearly a year in a house in Holbrook, Long Island, with Keith Spencer, co-producing.
years.xp:
"Best day of my life," Crutchfield told Grantland of signing to Merge, a day spent hanging out and getting drunk with the band. She also said songs that once took an hour now take months.

The album hit No. 15 on the US Indie chart. Pitchfork gave it 8.1, and Rolling Stone put it at No. 15 of 2015.

years.h: Out in the Storm is a breakup record with a rhythm section
years.p: Recorded live at Miner Street in Philadelphia with John Agnello (Dinosaur Jr., Sonic Youth) and a full band including Allison Crutchfield on keyboards.
years.xp: The band: Allison, Katie Harkin, Katherine Simonetti on bass and Ashley Arnwine on drums. The album peaked at No. 7 on the US Indie chart. Pitchfork gave it 8.2 and ranked it No. 13 on its Best Rock Albums list of 2017.

years.h: Waxahatchee opens for Jawbreaker at Brooklyn Steel
years.p: She also supports them at the Hollywood Palladium on March 10, the band's first Los Angeles shows in 22 years.

years.h: Primavera 2018 is the low point that ends her drinking
years.p: Crutchfield has said she hit bottom at Barcelona's Primavera Sound, and the turn became the opening song "Oxbow" on Saint Cloud.
years.xp: She was 29 when she got sober. She told Grammy.com in 2024 that drinking "had a weight to it that it didn't have for everyone I knew." She also told Billboard in 2020 that Saint Cloud was largely about stopping.

years.h: Great Thunder EP: the stopgap that charts higher than it should
years.p: A Merge EP between albums, it reaches No. 26 on the US Indie chart and No. 6 on Heatseekers.

eras.title: Sober, and sounding like it
eras.text: A quieter record, a country turn and a pandemic that made her the year's most unavoidable voice. Recording moves to Texas and New York with a new producer, Brad Cook.

years.h: Saint Cloud: Sonic Ranch, Long Pond and a Brad Cook debut
years.p: Recorded in summer 2019 at Sonic Ranch in Texas and Long Pond in New York, the record lands as lockdown begins.
years.xp:
Pitchfork gave it 8.7 and ranked it No. 2 of 2020, the same spot Paste gave it. Rolling Stone put it No. 7, and it won Best Country Record at the 2021 Libera Awards.

Lead single "Fire" arrived in January. Crutchfield called it an anthem for self-acceptance.

years.h: Waxahatchee plays one full album a week from home
years.p: With tours cancelled, she runs a livestream series, each show covering one album.

years.h: "Lilacs" gets its own video and reaches adult alternative radio
years.p: The song charts on the AAA format, No. 26 on one list.

years.h: Waxahatchee writes the soundtrack for Apple TV+'s El Deafo
years.p: The kids' series soundtrack comes out on Apple Video Programming and Merge.

q: It was the big pivotal moment for me and Brad.
years.h: Brad Cook flies [[MJ Lenderman|4f52595e-652d-4894-95ea-f925234629fc]] to Sonic Ranch
years.p: Producer Brad Cook brings the guitarist to the sessions, and the harmonies on "Right Back to It" become the record.
years.xp: Crutchfield met Lenderman at SXSW. She said the harmony moment was "the big pivotal moment for me and Brad."

years.h: Plains: Katie and Jess Williamson go full country
years.p: Met through Kevin Morby in 2017, the two write separately through lockdown and release one album on Anti- with [[MJ Lenderman|4f52595e-652d-4894-95ea-f925234629fc]] on the tour.
years.xp: Plains was billed as a one-off. The record draws on 1990s pop-country and classic country.

eras.title: Tigers Blood
eras.text: Crutchfield and producer Brad Cook return to Sonic Ranch, add a guest guitarist and make the record critics rank all year.

yt: Right Back to It (feat. MJ Lenderman)
years.h: "Right Back to It" is the lead single, with a rowboat on Caddo Lake
years.p: Shot at Caddo Lake in Texas, the video puts Crutchfield and Lenderman singing in a rowboat, an idea she'd had for over a decade.
years.xp: Her team had called the idea a logistical nightmare. It was inspired by the Lemonheads' "Mrs. Robinson" video. Pitchfork called the song Best New Track and ranked it No. 2 of its 100 best songs of 2024, and the pair played it on The Late Show with Stephen Colbert.

years.h: Tigers Blood is Pitchfork's No. 6 album of 2024
years.p: Anti- releases the record; Pitchfork gave it 8.8 and Best New Music, then ranked it No. 6 of the year.
years.xp:
Brad Cook produced at Sonic Ranch. Lenderman played electric guitar throughout, Phil Cook handled banjo, Dobro and organ, and Spencer Tweedy played drums. Metacritic landed at 89. Consequence and Exclaim! both put it No. 3 of the year; Uncut had it No. 10.

Crutchfield told Grammy.com she wrote the songs over about six months, many of the lyrics on the road, and chose to "depend solely on the songs" rather than reinvent the sound.

years.h: The North American tour plays 2,500-seat theaters, not arenas
years.p: Crutchfield turns down bigger rooms to keep the shows intimate.

years.h: First Grammy nomination, for Best Americana Album
years.p: Rolling Stone reported it as her first nod after more than a decade of records.

eras.title: Sisters again: Snocaps
eras.text: The twins reunite on record, Crutchfield lends her voice to other people's songs, and Waxahatchee keeps going.

years.h: Snocaps: Katie and Allison finally make a record together
years.p: A teaser turns into a surprise Anti- album with both Crutchfields sharing lead vocals, MJ Lenderman on multiple instruments and Brad Cook producing.

years.h: She sings on Courtney Barnett's "Site Unseen"
years.p: Crutchfield is a featured artist on the single.
